title: Popular Culture in Japan
description: Examines popular culture in present-day Japan: advertising, music, fashion, television, animation, comics, sports. Integrates visual and acoustic material.

title: Body and Self in Japanese Culture
description: Addresses how historians, anthropologists, artists, creators of popular culture, film makers, and literary authors have attached meanings to the human body and its relation to selfhood since the 19th century.

title: Religion in Japanese Culture
description: A historical analysis of the major components of the classical and medieval religious systems of Japan, through investigation of texts, rituals, and institutions.

title: Seminar in Traditional Japanese Theater
description: Survey and in-depth examinations of specific selected topics in traditional Japanese theater. Knowledge of Japanese not required.

title: Shinto: Concepts and Practices in History
description: Course presents the variety of religious and cultural phenomena associated with Shinto in Japan through a survey of doctrinal developments throughout history, description of practices, and considerations on the relationship between Shinto and other religions and intellectual systems such as Buddhism, Daoism, Confucianism, and Christianity.

title: Shinto through the Ages
description: Explores the diversity of the Shinto tradition through an analysis of representative original texts in English translation ranging from ancient mythology (Kojiki, Nihon shoki, and Fudoki) and medieval syncretic discourses, to modern forms of Shinto nationalism.

title: Advanced Readings in Japanese Texts
description: Readings in Japanese texts on religion (Buddhism and Shinto) and intellectual history. The course focuses on an accurate understanding of linguistic representation of concepts and stylistic nuances in the fields of Japanese religious and cultural history.
prerequisites_raw: Japan 144 and 145 or prior approval of instructor

title: Special Topics in Japanese Studies
description: Special topics in Japanese Studies. Course content varies.

title: Asia and Italy: From the Silk Road to WEIBO
description: Students study a wide variety of texts and images related to the exchangesboth cultural and materialbetween China, Japan, and Italy, from Marco Polo's journey along the Silk Road to today's Eastern and Western hypermodernity.

title: Death, Love & Money in Modern Japan
description: How does capitalism remake intimacy and love? How does intimate kinship shape the experiences of aging and death? What kind of relationship exists between family and economy? Students explore these key questions by examining the theoretical texts about our life under capitalism jointly with the case studies from modern and contemporary Japan. The assigned materials will include readings, movies, and other visual-audio materials.

title: Imagining Edo/Tokyo
description: An interdisciplinary exploration of the city formerly known as Edo, and now known as Tokyo, from the nineteenth century to the present. Sources include literature, films, maps, photographs, and woodblock prints. All readings will be in English translation; no knowledge of Japanese is required.

title: Special Topics in Japanese Studies
description: Special topics in Japanese Studies. Course content varies.

title: Youth and Social Change in Contemporary Japan
description: Examines the lives of youth and young adults in Japan, particularly their struggles with, adaptations to, and active involvement in social change. Discussion topics include generational conflict, gender, family, employment, marginalization, migration, resistance, activism and media representation.

title: Media and Japanese Society
description: Examines different forms of media and their influence on society starting with a brief historical overview and then focusing on postwar to contemporary media including music, film, computer games/anime, and the internet including social media.

title: Shamanism in the Japanese Archipelago
description: Considers the term shaman and its application to diverse traditions in the Japanese archipelago. After exploring definitions and theories of shamanism, we examine historical and contemporary shamanic traditions among the Japanese, Ainu, and Okinawan cultures.

title: Japanese TV: History, Genres, and Content
description: Surveys the history of Japanese TV and the development of the most important genres, including rom-com, detective drama, and variety shows. We will analyze content for how they depict social issues, including work culture, gender, and conflict resolution.

title: Women and Womanhood in Japanese History
description: From rulers to entertainers, court ladies to feminists, women in Japanese history were defined by and responded to their various societal roles. Examining texts by and about diverse women, we reconsider the history of Japan through the lens of gender.

title: Women's Literature in Japan
description: This course surveys various genres of women's literature and other artistic expressions (i.e. film, comic essay, and performance art) by contemporary women in Japan. By doing so, it introduces issues of gender and sexuality in postwar Japanese society and some of the major cultural analyses and discourses around the issues.

title: Introduction to Classical Japanese
description: Introduction to classical Japanese grammar, vocabulary, and major genres. Foundation for the study of premodern through prewar texts. Prerequisite for JAPAN 183.

title: Readings in Premodern through Meiji Japanese Texts
description: Selected readings in medieval, early modern, and Meiji texts.

title: Senior Honors Project
description: An independent study course (one to three quarters) directed by a faculty member with a carefully chosen topic and bibliography which will result in a documented project or a senior thesis.
prerequisites_raw: Open to senior majors only; consent of instructor.

title: Readings in Japanese
description: Guided reading in Japanese on a subject not covered in the regularly offered courses.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Japaneseconsent of instructor.

title: Independent Studies in Japanese
description: Individual investigations in literary fields.
prerequisites_raw: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in Japanese; at least one of those two courses taken with instructor for Japan 199; GPA for those two courses 3.5 or higher

title: Independent Research Assistance
description: Faculty supervised research.
prerequisites_raw: Completion of at least 2 upper-division courses in Japanese studies or EastAsian Cultural Studies; consent of instructor and department.

title: Readings in Selected Texts
description: Course will center on readings of japanese texts type and period to depend on needs of students and wishes of instructor. Research methods to be taught as appropriate.
prerequisites_raw: Ability to read japanese at graduate level; consent of instructor. Normallygraduate status is required.

title: Bibliography and Research Methodology
description: Introduction to bibliographies, reference works, and methodologies of research in japanese studies.

title: Japan Modern
description: Examines Japanese modernity from the mid-nineteenth century to today and analyzes theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of modern Japanese history and society.

title: Representation in Japanese and European Drama
description: A comparative study of theoretical and critical texts that address representation in drama, with particular attention to ideas about imitation and realism, character development, and audience/actor relationships. We will study a range of texts from Japanese and European theater history.

title: Transnational Japanese Studies
description: The broad goal of this seminar is to teach graduate students how to utilize theory to produce scholarly knowledge. Specifically, it introduces theories pertinent to the study of diaspora, globalization, and transnationalism with a focus on empirical research about Japan.

title: Anthropology of Japan
description: This course focuses on the history, methods, theories, and politics pertaining to the anthropological study of Japan. It primarily covers the postwar academic texts in English, and occasionally engages sources in Japanese, in alternative formats, and/or from earlier historical periods.
